title: No test for scan() with truncated begin-base64 (no ==== terminator)
description:
scan.rs handle_block() skips past a begin-base64 block by advancing until it finds '====' or EOF (lines 175-187). The case where EOF is reached without finding '====' is untested.

Missing test scenario:
  Input: 'begin-base64 644 file.txt\naGVsbG8=\n' (no ==== terminator, no further content)

Expected behavior per the code: scan_pos reaches input.len(), the while-loop exits naturally, *pos = scan_pos = input.len(). One Err(BeginBase64) is emitted and the outer scan loop terminates.

Risk: If the no-==== path has a bug (e.g. off-by-one causing scan_pos > input.len() which would panic on the next &input[scan_pos..] slice), it would only be discovered in production.

Fix: Add a test for scan_impl() on a begin-base64 block without a ==== terminator. Assert: exactly one Err(BeginBase64) result, no panic, no subsequent blocks dropped.
